data.title: Ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden probes
data.description:
Key points:
  • Complaint alleges ex-officials falsely claimed little knowledge of Hunter Biden probe
  • Floris' lawyers call case politically motivated
  • Case centers on FBI's response to Hunter Biden laptop in 2020

By Andrew Goudsward

The US Justice Department has charged two former senior FBI officials with lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations into former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter, according to court documents made public on Friday.

Nikki Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, who each held senior counterintelligence roles at the FBI, were charged in federal court in Washington. They allegedly misled a House of Representatives panel about the role of an FBI foreign influence task force in investigations into Hunter Biden, according to a criminal complaint.

The case marks the latest attempt by the Justice Department to investigate and prosecute US officials over incidents that angered President Donald Trump and his allies.

Floris and Benavides served in leading roles on the FBI foreign influence task force, a group aimed at combating attempts to influence US elections that was disbanded during the second Trump administration after facing criticism from Republicans.

The officials briefed two Republican senators in 2020, warning them of US intelligence concerns that some allegations against Hunter Biden were part of a Russian influence operation, according to prior media reports.

Lawyers for Floris condemned the case on Friday as the latest in a string of politically motivated prosecutions by the DOJ under the Trump administration.

"The government’s reasons for charging Nikki are as transparent as they are unjust: to push a false narrative for a shot at political points," Floris' lawyers said in a statement.

A lawyer for Benavides did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system, but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them," US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro wrote in a social media post.

Floris and Benavides made an initial court appearance on Friday. A federal grand jury in Washington will have to approve an indictment for the case to move forward.

A TRUMP GRIEVANCE

The case centers on an issue that has long been a focus of Trump and his allies: the FBI's handling of a laptop purportedly belonging to Hunter Biden that surfaced in the weeks leading up to the 2020 election, which Trump lost to Joe Biden.

The criminal complaint alleges that Floris and Benavides lied to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 testimony where they each claimed little knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigation and the laptop episode. It alleges that Floris and Benavides were in contact with members of the Hunter Biden investigative team in 2020 and took part in the FBI's response to public reporting on the laptop.

Benavides told the House panel that he learned about the Hunter Biden probes through searching on Wikipedia, according to the complaint.

Hunter Biden was later charged with federal gun and tax-related crimes during his father's administration. Joe Biden pardoned his son shortly before leaving office.

Trump and his allies have long claimed that the FBI, during Trump's first term, and social media companies, suppressed the laptop story to protect Joe Biden's campaign. The case against Floris and Benavides does not make that allegation.

The DOJ under Trump has also investigated the US intelligence community's finding that Russia sought to aid Trump's 2016 campaign and the FBI raid of Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort for classified documents in 2022. That probe has been mired in staff turmoil.

The DOJ has also brought charges against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly lying to Congress about media leaks, a case that was later dismissed, and for allegedly threatening Trump in a social media post that featured seashells arranged to form the numbers "86 47."

data.title: Initia halts network after security incident as attacker reportedly mints tokens
data.description:
Initia, a blockchain built to support interconnected chains, halted its layer 1 blockchain and rollups on Friday after a security incident.

Blockchain researcher Spreek initially estimated that the attacker had cashed out roughly $2.6 million and had more funds in transit. Onchain data shows a single transfer of approximately 1,135 ETH worth more than $2.7 million.

Initia said it was investigating the reach of the incident alongside security teams, validators and exchanges. It has not confirmed the amount lost.

Initia's native INIT token fell 14% immediately after the exploit was reported, before reversing the losses. The token is now up 14% on the day.

data.title: Iovance’s Melanoma Therapy Shows Promising 4-Year Data – Retail Says Acquisition Imminent Before 2027-End
data.description:
Key points:
  • The trial evaluated 24 patients who received a single infusion of Lifileucel with Merck’s Keytruda.
  • The trial showed a complete response rate of 29.2%.
  • The company expects its cash position to fund operations into the second half of 2028.

Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) was in the spotlight on Friday after the biotech firm reported promising results from a Phase 2 trial of its experimental cell therapy Lifileucel, combined with Merck’s (MRK) Keytruda, in patients with advanced melanoma.

IOVA shares were down 1.1% at the time of writing, tracking the broader selloff in biotech stocks. The State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) was also down 1.1%.

Median Overall Survival Not Reached After More Than Four Years Of Follow-Up

The company said its Phase 2 IOV-COM-202 trial evaluated 24 patients who received a single infusion of Lifileucel with Keytruda. The results showed an objective response rate (ORR) of 62.5%, meaning nearly two-thirds of patients experienced significant tumor shrinkage or disappearance.

The trial also showed a complete response (CR) rate of 29.2%, indicating nearly a third of the patients had no detectable signs of cancer following treatment.

Crucially, the median overall survival had not been reached after a median follow-up of 50.9 months. Lifileucel already received accelerated U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in February 2024.

“The final Cohort 1A results demonstrate unprecedented efficacy and a potentially best-in-class clinical profile for Lifileucel combined with Pembrolizumab in frontline advanced melanoma,” said Noah Berkowitz, Chief Medical Officer at Iovance.

Iovance will present the first clinical data for Lifileucel in soft tissue sarcomas on October 26.

IOVA’s Pipeline In Focus

Iovance’s pipeline also includes studies in lung, endometrial and soft tissue cancers. The FDA recently granted Fast Track designation for Lifileucel in certain soft tissue sarcomas.

The company had about $304 million in cash, investments and restricted cash as of June 30, 2026, which it expects will fund its operations into the second half of 2028.

Retail Says IOVA To Be Acquired By End Of 2027

data.title: Stock Market Today: Dow Slides as Oil Prices Climb to Highest in Five Months — WSJ
data.description:
By Ed Ballard

Oil prices continue to climb as concerns mount that the U.S.-Iran conflict could soon escalate, sending stocks lower.

Brent crude is poised to close today at its highest level since April. The U.S. is sending additional forces to the Middle East, and Iran warned it would strike civilian targets in neighboring countries if the U.S. and Israel restart their air campaign.

The Dow slid about 500 points, while the Nasdaq pared losses and turned higher, a sign the AI rout could be moderating after yesterday's selloff.

Still, signs of stress in the AI trade continued overnight, with SK Hynix yanking the planned U.S. IPO of its memory-chip business. The Korean chipmaker has been among the AI boom's chief beneficiaries.

Treasury yields are rebounding somewhat after an investor flight for safety led to the largest one-day decline in 3 ½ years yesterday.

data.title: SA Asks: Why did the market sell off after relatively good earnings reports?
data.description:
Why did the market sell off this week after the release of relatively good earnings reports?

Seeking Alpha analysts Jack Bowman and Gytis Zizys offer their views.

Jack Bowman: With the recent drama surrounding CoreWeave , the bell seems to be tolling for return on invested capital metrics. Top and bottom line beats, like with Tesla , aren't meaningful if the market is suspecting that you're using that to plow straight into more capex without seeing the return.

I don't know if this trend will hold. I think that hyperscaler earnings, especially those of Microsoft and Alphabet , which both report on Oct. 28, will determine market sentiment from here. If they're good, not just in the top and bottom lines, but also in cloud revenue growth, then I'd assume the bulls will come back. Miss those figures, and it may be rough sailing until mid-November, when Nvidia earnings come out.

Gytis Zizys: I think the main reason we are seeing such brutal price action, specifically in the Nasdaq and the S&P500 to an extent, is because investors fear the AI growth narrative has seemingly run its course. Multiple companies reported increased demand across the board when it comes to AI growth; Taiwan Semiconductor and Micron have reported stellar earnings, but the sentiment is that it’s time to put the brakes on.

The constant news around the U.S. and Iran flip-flopping isn’t helping the narrative, either.

I don’t think the growth is over. At least that’s not what the fundamental picture of many companies that reported is saying. Meta Platforms just reported great earnings, and capex spending will just increase next year. Other hyperscalers will follow suit.

It is also important to note that the picture looks worse than it is because the correction has mainly hit tech stocks, while most other sectors are faring much better. There’s too much concentration in AI names these days that is distorting the picture.

Reveille [AQSE: REV], a uranium exploration and development company with a primary focus on Italy's largest uranium deposits, announces that its Non-Executive Chairman, The Hon. Michael R. Pompeo, former US Secretary of State and CIA Director, has participated in an interview with Jeremy Naylor.

Notes to Editors

Reveille Resources plc (AQSE: REV) is a UK natural resources exploration and development company with a primary focus on Italy, where it is advancing the exploration and development of the country's largest historic uranium deposits.

Through its Italian subsidiary, Futuro Energetico Italiano S.r.l, the Company has submitted exploration-licence applications in respect of the Novazza and Val Vedello uranium projects in northern Italy, each of which is subject to the applicable environmental-assessment process. The projects were historically explored and developed by AGIP Nucleare S.p.A. and its operating subsidiary, SOMIREN, both part of the ENI group, during Italy's national nuclear programme between 1959 and 1983. This work included more than 87,000 metres of historical drilling and approximately 17 kilometres of underground development.

Reveille's strategy is to identify and advance uranium projects that have benefited from substantial historical exploration and technical work, but where value has yet to be fully realised due to geopolitical, technological, financial or historical factors. By applying modern exploration techniques and internationally recognised reporting standards, the Company intends to verify historical data, advance exploration and work towards the delineation of mineral resources in accordance with internationally recognised reporting standards.

While Italy remains the Company's principal area of focus, Reveille will selectively evaluate additional uranium opportunities elsewhere in Europe and in other Western jurisdictions where similar value creation opportunities exist. The Company is committed to advancing its projects responsibly, working closely with local communities, regulators and other stakeholders to ensure that exploration activities are undertaken to the highest environmental, technical and governance standards.

data.title: Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March
data.description:
By Nushaiba Iqbal

The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.

Inflation rose to 3.1% in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest business outlook survey showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination.

Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be revised higher, BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming.

Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem.

"What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins.

"So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming."

Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year.

This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027.

Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday.

Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years.

But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led war with Iran that began in February.

Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is widely expected to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates.

But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy.

Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.”

Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% in Q2 and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found.

Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed.

(Other stories from the Reuters global economic poll)
